title: How do we write 234 tenths as a decimal?
description: A count of tenths and hundredths is written as a fraction, split by place and then written as a decimal. Keeko's doubt is that the point goes in front of the digits.
teaching_notes: One idea: a count of tenths is that count divided by ten, and a count of hundredths is that count divided by a hundred. Watch for students who put the point in front of all the digits.

source: Write 234 tenths in decimal form. Then write (a) 234 hundredths and (b) 105 tenths.
video_script.why: The child writes fractions with one digit as decimals and now writes a large count of tenths or hundredths.
video_script.substitution: A count of tenths is the count over ten, and the whole number part comes from the full tens of tenths.
video_script.anchor: a count of tenths and hundredths written as a fraction
video_script.wrong_move: puts the point in front of all the digits
video_script.payoff_line: Divide the count by ten for tenths, and by a hundred for hundredths

final_answer.spoken: two hundred thirty four tenths is twenty three point four; the hundredths make two point three four and the other tenths make ten point five

video_script.fraction_reading: tenths and hundredths are said as words
maths_rules: the slip: 0.234 is 234 thousandths, not 234 tenths
video_script.design: A count of tenths is written as a fraction over ten in the working band, split by place and joined. Keeko's doubt puts a point in front of the digits.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book, then 234 tenths; 234 hundredths and 105 tenths wait beside it; a question mark in the anchor band
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a large count of tenths.
<bookmark mark='count'/>We have two hundred thirty-four tenths, and then two hundred thirty-four hundredths and one hundred five tenths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each one in decimal form.

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits beside it as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: ten tenths fill one unit bar; 234 tenths shown as 23 full bars and 4 tenths

marks.bar: a unit bar shows ten tenths
marks.many: bars are stacked to show 23 full bars and 4 tenths

narration: <bookmark mark='bar'/>Ten tenths fill one whole unit bar.
<bookmark mark='many'/>A large count of tenths makes many full units, and a few tenths are left over.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three counts of tenths and hundredths.

beats.on_screen: To find: each count in decimal form
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each count in decimal form.

marks.split: the top is split into 200, 30 and 4

narration: <bookmark mark='frac'/>Step one, write two hundred thirty-four tenths as two hundred thirty-four over ten.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Split the top into two hundred, thirty and four. Two hundred tenths is twenty, and thirty tenths is three.
<bookmark mark='join'/>That is twenty plus three plus four tenths, which is twenty-three point four.

marks.split: the top is split into 200, 30 and 4

narration: <bookmark mark='frac'/>Step two, write two hundred thirty-four hundredths as two hundred thirty-four over one hundred.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Split the top again. Two hundred hundredths is two, and thirty hundredths is three tenths.
<bookmark mark='join'/>That is two plus three tenths plus four hundredths, which is two point three four.

marks.split: the top is split into 100 and 5

narration: <bookmark mark='frac'/>Step three, write one hundred five tenths as one hundred five over ten.
<bookmark mark='split'/>One hundred tenths is ten, and five tenths is left.
<bookmark mark='join'/>That is ten plus five tenths, which is ten point five.

marks.list: the three answers are marked in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Divide the count by ten for tenths, and by a hundred for hundredths.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Two hundred thirty-four tenths is twenty-three point four. The hundredths make two point three four, and one hundred five tenths make ten point five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the working
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 0.234 appears and is struck out; 234/10 is divided by ten and the point moves one place left; 23.4 is written

marks.fix: 0.234 is struck out and the point is placed after the 23

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is zero point two three four, because the point goes in front.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But dividing by ten moves the point only one place left. Two hundred thirty-four tenths is twenty-three point four.
